# Pi magic 8-ball: V1 contract and design

## Contents

- [Design](#design)
- [Contract](#contract)
- [Verification and remaining limits](#verification)


## Design {#design}

V1 adds one advisory choice tool. It uses a separate chat-model loop to collect neutral state, then Pi's classifier API.
Jev and Clef use the same backend boundary. Model selection stays in extension-owned settings files and user-issued slash commands, not model-issued arguments.
The builder has no inherited extensions, filesystem writes, shell, web, or classifier access. Its transcript stays in memory.
The parent session stores returned state and results through normal Pi tool-result persistence. Configured providers receive permitted context and state.
Read scopes restrict collection, not provider retention. Users must select providers suitable for their data.
Prompt instructions request neutrality. Schema validation cannot prove neutrality, factual accuracy, completeness, or secret removal.

Implementation safety ceilings are 4 builder requests, 8 evidence calls, 2048 output tokens per builder request, and 120000 milliseconds per invocation.
These ceilings bound work, not monetary cost or confidence calibration. The extension makes no application-level retries or model fallbacks.
Conversation input holds at most 24000 UTF-8 bytes. A workspace result holds at most 16000 UTF-8 bytes.
State holds at most 12000 UTF-8 bytes. Truncation is explicit. Oversized or malformed final state fails closed.
Git execution, research, boolean questions, and score questions are outside V1.

## Contract {#contract}

`magic8ball({ question, responses, abstain?, context? })` returns a structured success or error.
`context` has boolean `conversation` and `workspace` fields. Both default to true. Unknown fields and non-booleans are invalid.
`abstain` defaults to true. Explicit false disables the added `insufficient_evidence` response.
Both configured models require provider and model identifiers. The extension never uses the parent model as a fallback.
User settings live in `<Pi agent directory>/magic8ball.json`, normally `~/.pi/agent/magic8ball.json`.
Trusted project settings live in `<cwd>/.pi/magic8ball.json`. Each role is a complete `{ "provider": "...", "model": "..." }` pair.
A project role overrides the entire user role. Partial pairs do not inherit individual fields. Untrusted project files are not read.
The four former `PI_MAGIC8BALL_*` model-selection variables are ignored. Provider credentials remain in Pi's authentication system.
`/magic8ball` opens an interactive two-model picker. `/magic8ball show` displays settings and their sources.
`/magic8ball builder <provider> <model>` and `/magic8ball classifier <provider> <model>` update one role.
A single `--project` or `--global` flag may precede or follow command arguments; saves default to user scope.
In noninteractive mode, `/magic8ball` displays usage and settings without writing. Picker cancellation never writes.

<a id="REQ-1"></a>

**REQ-1**

The tool MUST validate inputs before model calls. The question and every response description MUST be nonempty strings after trimming.
Response identifiers MUST match `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,63}` and exclude `__proto__`, `prototype`, `constructor`, and `insufficient_evidence`.
The caller MUST supply 2–25 responses with abstention, or 2–26 without it. The tool MUST preserve identifiers and descriptions.
The serialized request MUST contain at most 16000 UTF-8 bytes. Invalid domain inputs MUST return `invalid-input` without model calls.
Pi's schema-validation error takes precedence when arguments fail the registered parameter schema before the extension executes.


<a id="AC-1"></a>

**AC-1**

Changed behavior. Valid inputs retain caller criteria and add abstention by default. Explicit false permits 26 caller choices.
Empty descriptions, reserved identifiers, invalid counts, unknown fields, and oversized requests produce `invalid-input` before model calls.


<a id="REQ-2"></a>

**REQ-2**

The builder MUST run before classification with only the permitted conversation and workspace scopes.
It MUST receive neutral-state instructions and only the three evidence tools when workspace scope is true.
It MUST NOT receive classifier output from this invocation or prior `magic8ball` tool results.
Final state MUST contain exactly `goal`, `constraints`, `current_state`, `evidence`, and `uncertainties`.
Evidence entries MUST contain exactly nonempty `fact` and `source` strings. Other collections MUST contain only nonempty strings.
The tool MUST reject candidate-keyed state, malformed JSON, extra fields, or state exceeding 12000 bytes as `invalid-state`.


<a id="AC-2"></a>

**AC-2**

Changed behavior. Mock builder and classifier calls show state precedes classification and no classifier feedback reaches the builder.
Workspace-disabled requests expose no evidence tools. Conversation-disabled requests expose no prior messages.
Valid state reaches classification unchanged. Extra recommendation fields, candidate-keyed state, malformed JSON, and oversized state fail before classification.


<a id="REQ-3"></a>

**REQ-3**

The three evidence tools MUST restrict paths to the real workspace root and reject symlinks and special files.
They MUST reject dot-prefixed path segments, `node_modules`, and conventional credential files, including PEM, key, and P12 files.
Listing MUST omit denied paths. Read and literal search MUST operate on one regular UTF-8 text file per call.
Read offset defaults to 1. Read limit defaults to 200 and MUST be in the inclusive range 1–200.
List results MUST contain at most 200 names. Search results MUST contain at most 200 matching lines.
File content inspection MUST read at most 16000 bytes per call. Truncation MUST be explicit.
The builder MUST call evidence tools through `ctx.executeTool` so Pi's validation and permission hooks remain active.
These tools MUST NOT write files, execute workspace code, or invoke other tools.


<a id="AC-3"></a>

**AC-3**

Changed behavior. Temporary-workspace tests confirm bounded read, list, and literal search.
Traversal, external paths, symlinks, hidden credential paths, key files, binary files, and special files fail without exposing content.
Builder tests show only allowlisted evidence names reach the nested-tool boundary. Permission failures stop classification.


<a id="REQ-4"></a>

**REQ-4**

The classifier adapter MUST use the configured catalog entry and Pi's `choice` interface for both Jev and Clef.
A success MUST return `answer`, `probabilities`, backend `confidence`, `abstained`, `advisory: true`, state, models, collection metadata, and usage.
The distribution MUST contain exactly the supplied identifiers, including added abstention. Every probability and confidence MUST be finite and in [0,1].
The probability sum MUST differ from 1 by no more than 0.000001. The selected identifier MUST have maximal probability.
The adapter MUST preserve the backend's choice among tied maxima. It MUST NOT renormalize probabilities or substitute confidence.
A malformed answer MUST return `invalid-answer`. Classifier failures MUST return `classifier-failed` without a decision.


<a id="AC-4"></a>

**AC-4**

Changed behavior. Mock Jev and Clef entries receive identical typed questions and state.
Successful results preserve all probabilities and confidence, including confidence different from winning probability and tied choices.
Missing, extra, negative, nonfinite, unnormalized, or nonmaximal answers fail. Abstention is reported without becoming an execution command.


<a id="REQ-5"></a>

**REQ-5**

The orchestrator MUST stop on cancellation, timeout, builder failure, permission failure, or exhausted request or tool ceilings.
It MUST propagate one combined abort signal to builder requests, evidence tools, and classification.
It MUST return an error without a fabricated answer and retain usage reported by completed model calls, including failed calls.
A valid effective settings object that lacks either model role MUST produce `not-configured` before builder requests. An unavailable catalog entry MUST produce `model-unavailable`.
Invalid settings and access failures are governed by REQ-7.
The builder MUST be a physical chat-model entry. A Pi virtual-model entry MUST produce `model-unavailable` before model requests.
No application-level retry, automatic repair, hidden model fallback, background process, or separate transcript file is permitted.
Provider-level retry suppression uses `maxRetries: 0` where supported. Provider adapters can have their own transport behavior.


<a id="AC-5"></a>

**AC-5**

Changed behavior. Fault-injection tests exercise missing configuration, unavailable models, builder and classifier failures, cancellation, timeout, and budget exhaustion.
A configured virtual builder model produces `model-unavailable` before any builder or classifier call.
No classifier call follows a builder failure. No request or tool call exceeds its ceiling. Completed-call usage survives errors.


<a id="REQ-6"></a>

**REQ-6**

The package MUST register `magic8ball` as a model-only tool with a structured output schema.
Evidence tools MUST be callable nested tools, inactive by default, with read-only annotations.
The main tool description and each success MUST identify decisions as advisory and confidence as distribution concentration, not correctness probability.
The extension MUST work without terminal UI and MUST return aggregate nested-model usage in Pi's tool result.


<a id="AC-6"></a>

**AC-6**

Changed behavior. Load the extension against installed Pi without network calls or UI.
Inspect registration, schemas, tool annotations, advisory guidance, structured success and error results, and Pi usage accounting.
Run mocked model calls through the registered main and evidence tools. Verify host-selected Jev and Clef paths.


<a id="REQ-7"></a>

**REQ-7**

Model selection MUST come only from `magic8ball.json` in Pi's agent directory and, when `ctx.isProjectTrusted()` is true, the current workspace's `.pi` directory.
Settings MUST contain only optional `builder` and `classifier` roles. Each present role MUST contain exactly nonempty `provider` and `model` strings with no whitespace; each identifier MUST contain at most 512 UTF-8 bytes.
Project settings MUST replace complete roles, not merge individual fields. A missing file MUST act as an empty settings layer.
Each invocation MUST read a fresh settings snapshot before resolving either model. Missing effective roles MUST return `not-configured` before model requests.
Malformed JSON, invalid fields, or files exceeding 16000 UTF-8 bytes MUST return `invalid-config`; inaccessible files, symlink targets or immediate parent directories, and nonregular files MUST return `settings-unavailable`.
Settings failure MUST NOT fall back to environment variables, the parent model, or another settings layer. Untrusted project files MUST be ignored without opening them.


<a id="AC-7"></a>

**AC-7**

Changed behavior. Temporary-file tests verify user settings, complete project-role precedence, missing roles, and fresh reads after manual edits.
Old model-selection environment variables do not configure an empty settings file.
Untrusted malformed project files are ignored; trusted malformed, oversized, partial-pair, unknown-field, symlink, and nonregular files fail before any model call.
Preserved behavior. Configured physical builders, Jev and Clef still use the same model boundary, usage accounting, and error handling as AC-5 and AC-6.


<a id="REQ-8"></a>

**REQ-8**

The extension MUST register a user-issued `/magic8ball` command with interactive configuration, display, and explicit builder/classifier subcommands.
Saves MUST default to user scope; `--project` MUST require current project trust. Conflicting or repeated scope flags and malformed command arguments MUST fail without writes.
The picker MUST expose physical available chat models for the builder and available classifier entries for the classifier. Explicit identifiers MUST resolve to the same model types before persistence.
Cancelling either picker MUST leave both files unchanged. Noninteractive invocation without identifiers MUST NOT prompt or write.
Successful saves MUST preserve the other role in the selected layer and use a same-directory temporary file followed by atomic replacement.
Writes MUST serialize through Pi's file-mutation queue and an exclusive lock file. Contention with another process, corrupt existing settings, or detected external modification MUST fail rather than overwrite data.
A command MUST report its saved path and effective selections, including project overrides of user settings. The next tool invocation MUST use saved settings without `/reload`.
The command MUST NOT change Pi's active conversation model, store credentials, or issue generation or classification requests. Catalog availability uses Pi's normal authentication boundary.
Filesystem races with nonparticipating writers and power-loss durability are outside the guarantee. A save error with uncertain outcome MUST direct the user to inspect settings before retrying.


<a id="AC-8"></a>

**AC-8**

Changed behavior. Invoke the registered command against temporary directories and mock model catalogs/UI.
Verify interactive configuration, user and trusted-project role updates, picker cancellation at each stage, display, invalid syntax/models, noninteractive behavior, denied project writes, and immediate tool use.
Concurrent in-process role updates preserve both roles. Existing lock files and corrupt settings prevent replacement. Successful writes leave no owned temporary or lock files.
Assert configuration performs no model request, does not change the active model, and does not alter unrelated Pi settings files.


<a id="REQ-9"></a>

**REQ-9**

In TUI mode, each model picker MUST use a viewport bounded by the current terminal height.
The selected model MUST remain visible during keyboard navigation and terminal resize.
Each model MUST occupy one row. Display truncation MUST NOT change the selected provider or model identifier.
The picker MUST retain selection across resize. A terminal too short for all controls MUST prioritize the selected row.
RPC mode MUST continue to use the supported select dialog. Cancellation and settings persistence MUST retain REQ-8 behavior.


<a id="AC-9"></a>

**AC-9**

Changed behavior. Render each TUI picker with 100 models at 30 and 80 columns and 6, 10, 24, and 40 rows.
Navigate to the last model and resize the terminal. PASS if the selected row remains visible and the picker fits.
At one and three terminal rows, PASS if the selected row remains visible within the terminal height.
Render long Unicode identifiers. PASS if every line fits the width and selection saves the complete identifiers.
Preserved behavior. RPC selection, virtual-builder exclusion, cancellation at either stage, and noninteractive behavior retain AC-8 results.
Cancel each TUI picker after navigation. PASS if both settings files remain unchanged and no model request occurs.


<a id="REQ-10"></a>

**REQ-10**

Each TUI picker MUST use an inline layout with at most 10 model rows, like Pi's `/model` selector.
REQ-9 terminal-height bounds MUST take precedence when fewer rows fit.
The picker MUST support editable fuzzy search across the provider, model identifier, and display name.
Search MUST use Pi's fuzzyFilter token matching and ranking. A nonempty query edit MUST select the best match.
Arrow keys MUST wrap across filtered results. Other text keys, including `j` and `k`, MUST edit the search input.
The configured model for the current role MUST appear first before search and carry a current-selection marker.
When space permits, the picker MUST show the selected model's display name and navigation hints.
An empty result set MUST show `No matching models`. Enter with no match MUST NOT finish the picker.
Escape and Ctrl+C MUST cancel without writes. RPC MUST retain REQ-9 behavior.
The picker MUST preserve complete model identifiers and MUST NOT change Pi's conversation model or refresh remote catalogs.


<a id="AC-10"></a>

**AC-10**

Changed behavior. Open both 100-model catalogs in an 80-column, 60-row terminal.
PASS if the picker is inline and displays at most 10 model rows.
Type mixed-case fuzzy queries using display names and provider/model tokens. Edit and clear the query.
PASS if filtering matches Pi's ranking, selects the best match, and saves the complete selected identifiers.
Type `j` and `k`. PASS if these keys edit the query instead of navigating.
Start with configured role models. PASS if each appears first, is marked current, and shows its display name.
With no matches, press Enter then clear the query. PASS if Enter does not finish and editing restores results.
Verify Up and Down wrap across results. Cancel with Escape and Ctrl+C at either stage.
PASS if cancellation leaves both settings files unchanged and performs no generation or classification.
Preserved behavior. AC-9 height, resize, Unicode width, identifier preservation, RPC, and cancellation checks MUST continue to pass.

## Verification and remaining limits {#verification}


AC-7 and AC-8 change configuration. The existing 14 tests passed before this change and cover preserved AC-1–AC-6 behavior.
All nine new settings/command tests failed before implementation against the existing environment-based extension and callable settings scaffolds.
After implementation, `npm run verify` passed strict TypeScript checking and all 23 Node tests against Pi 1.0.4.
The installed Pi extension loader registered four tools and the `magic8ball` slash command without errors.
Settings tests use private temporary directories, scoped environment cleanup, and mock UI/model catalogs. They do not change live user or project settings.

| Criterion | Check names in tests | Before settings implementation | After settings implementation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| AC-1–AC-6 | original validation, neutral-state, evidence, distribution, fault, usage, and registration checks | Passed | Passed |
| AC-7 | role precedence, trust and fresh reads; ignored old environment; malformed settings; unsafe files | Failed | Passed |
| AC-8 | scoped saves and immediate use; picker; cancellation; invalid/noninteractive commands; concurrent saves and lock contention | Failed | Passed |

Historical V1 verification: all original 14 tests failed against callable no-op scaffolds before the first implementation.
A separate AC-3 assertion reproduced explicit null values bypassing evidence defaults; the helper now rejects those values.
The settings change updates configuration fixtures without weakening the original assertions about model behavior.
`docs_validate` reported no diagnostics and publication completed for the project output root when the new requirements were imported.
These statements report observed local checks, not authenticated verification records or policy approval.

Model responses and the nested-tool boundary are mocked. The tests use Pi's installed session projection and TypeBox schemas.
No live calibration check, live terminal check, or context-builder quality evaluation has run.
In-process write serialization and pre-existing lock contention are tested. External-editor races and interrupted/power-loss saves are not fault-injected.
The settings comparison detects changed bytes before replacement; nonparticipating writers can still race the final validation and filesystem operation.
Implementation and automated checks required no package installation, profile activation, live settings edit, or deployment.
Development began in an empty bare repository and linked orphan worktree.
Profile-wide extension checks do not apply to this independent project. This package uses its own `npm run verify` command.

The workspace path filter is not an OS sandbox. Concurrent filesystem mutation can race path validation.
The helper rejects known credential paths, but ordinary files and conversation can contain secrets.
Direct prior magic8ball results are omitted. Quotations and compaction summaries can still contain prior decisions or probabilities.
Configured providers determine external retention. The parent session stores returned state and results through normal Pi persistence.

- #REQ-5 references: [#REQ-7](#REQ-7)



Picker layout verification (AC-9): the original selector rendered 110 lines for 100 models in a 40-row terminal.
Long Unicode labels rendered 610 lines in a 10-row terminal. Both changed-behavior tests failed before the picker change.
The TUI cancellation check and all 23 existing checks passed before the change.
After the change, `npm run verify` passed strict TypeScript checking and all 26 tests against Pi 1.0.4.
The checks render the actual picker component with mock terminal dimensions and real SelectList behavior.
They cover both catalogs, keyboard navigation, terminal resize, Unicode width, complete saved identifiers, and cancellation at either stage.
RPC keeps the supported select dialog. The first AC-9 implementation used a bounded overlay and removed controls when only the selected row fit.
These checks do not establish live terminal appearance or mouse behavior. No provider request or live settings change occurred.


Compact search verification (AC-10): the user requested `/model` behavior instead of the screen-sized overlay.
The installed Pi 1.0.4 selector uses an inline layout, 10 model rows, Input, and fuzzyFilter.
Its constructor requires a chat-session ModelRuntime, which ExtensionCommandContext does not expose. Classifier catalogs require a separate model type.
The magic8ball picker uses the host's Input and fuzzyFilter primitives plus SelectList, without the host selector's remote refresh.
The four new AC-10 checks failed before implementation. Existing AC-9 and configuration checks passed before implementation.
The old picker displayed 53 model rows in a 60-row terminal and had no search or configured-role marker.
After implementation, `npm run verify` passed strict TypeScript checking and all 30 tests.
AC-10 checks cover inline placement, the 10-row cap, fuzzy names and provider/model queries, text editing, and configured-role selection.
They also cover no-match Enter, query clearing, wrapped navigation, and Ctrl+C cancellation at either stage.
AC-9 height, resize, Unicode, complete identifiers, Escape cancellation, and RPC checks remain passing.
The overlay-only assertion in the old UI fixture was replaced with AC-10's required inline-placement assertion.
These checks use mock terminal dimensions. They do not verify live terminal appearance or remote provider behavior.

After configuration, one user-requested live smoke call completed both the context builder and classifier stages.
The call used conversation context with workspace access disabled. It returned a valid advisory distribution without abstention.
This confirms that the loaded extension and configured providers completed one end-to-end call.
It does not establish calibration, context-builder quality, workspace evidence collection, or live terminal appearance.
Before initial GitHub publication, `npm run verify` again passed strict TypeScript checking and all 30 tests.
A scan of the 16 intended project files found no common credential patterns. This scan is not a secret-detection guarantee.
